```text
# PR #3174: Patch: the db (store contract) job builds the engine and the cards at opt-level 0, which cuts its compile

Closes #3162

`crates/server/tests/db/run.sh` now builds the engine and the cards at opt-level 0, which shortens the compile that made `db (store contract)` take 8m 39s. The full Postgres run passed locally. Whether the CI job drops under five minutes is untested here, because CI also counts checkout, toolchain and cache restore.

The test profile builds those two crates at opt-level 2 (`Cargo.toml`). The store tests read and write rows and play no game, so the optimization only costs compile time. A count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` cannot help, because there is no `db` table there and a count would not split the compile anyway.

## What changed

- **`crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`:** a new `PROFILE_FLAGS` variable sets `profile.test.package.jackioh-engine.opt-level=0` and the same for `jackioh-cards`, through `--config`. It goes to the `cargo build` and to `run_tests`' `cargo test`. `run_tests` covers both the `--list` call and the three shard runs, so no `cargo` call in the script is left without the flags. A comment above the variable gives the reason and the planner's measurements.
- **`crates/server/README.md`:** the "Tests" sentence about `tests/db/run.sh` now names the opt-level-0 build, the `PROFILE_FLAGS`, and #3162.

I followed the plan as written and did not depart from it. The ShellCheck suppressions are the two lines the plan gave: SC2086 is disabled where the flags are used, because they are several arguments on purpose.

## How I tested it

- `sh -n crates/server/tests/db/run.sh` printed nothing and exited 0.
- `shellcheck` on the file shows only the two warnings the file already had, SC1007 on the `REPO=` line and SC2329 on `cleanup()`. I ran it on the file from `HEAD` as well and got the same two, so there is no new warning and no SC2086.
- Docker was available, so I ran the real suite: `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`.
  - It exited with status 0.
  - The three shards printed `test result: ok. 228 passed`, `227 passed` and `227 passed`, which is all 682 `store::` tests.
  - The build step's `Finished` line says `1m 48s`. That is a cold build in this environment, including the dependencies. The three `cargo test` calls after it printed `Finished` in 0.37 s, 0.47 s and 0.41 s.
  - `awk '/--- cargo test/{f=1} f && /Compiling/{bad=1} END{exit bad}' /tmp/db.log` exited 0, so there is no `Compiling` line after the `--- cargo test` header. No `cargo` call is missing the flags.
- I ran nothing else from the harness's list. The change touches no Rust, spec, catalog, ruling or web code, and the plan noted that none of those checks read this script.

## Decisions

- **`DB_SHARDS` stays at 3.** The planner measured 6 and 8 databases on a warm build and the test phase stayed at about 50 s, so more shards only add load.
- **No `.github/` change.** Nothing there needs to change, so no person has to act.
- **Left alone, as the plan said:** the redundant `truncate` in `StoreHarness::postgres()`, since removing it means changing the test harness for about 50 ms per Postgres test.

## For the reviewer

- Every `cargo` call in `run.sh` has to take the same `$PROFILE_FLAGS`. A different profile is a different build, so a call without them rebuilds the workspace at opt-level 2, about three minutes. The `awk` check above catches that.
- Check the next `ci-duration` report to confirm the saving in CI. If the job is still over five minutes, the plan suggests looking at the db job's Rust cache first. A cold CI cache could add dependency compile time that nothing outside `.github/` can fix.

### Its own review

Built and checked on `claude-6`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

<details><summary>Rounds and checks</summary>

| Round | Builder | Checks | Review |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | build, 3.4 min | green | - |

| Gate | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| rustfmt (`cargo fmt --check`) | pass | 6s |
| catalog (`cargo jackioh catalog check`) | pass | 195s |
| patches (`cargo jackioh patches check`) | pass | 1s |
| rulings (`cargo jackioh spec check`) | pass | 2s |
| clippy (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`) | pass | 133s |
| cargo tests (`cargo test --workspace --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts && test -z "$(git status --porcelain -- apps/web/src/wire)"`) | pass | 1424s |
| web tests (`sh scripts/build-wasm.sh && pnpm exec vitest run --project web --changed origin/main --exclude '**/src/audio/**' --exclude '**/src/fx/**' --exclude '**/src/cards/art/convention.test.ts'`) | pass | 389s |

</details>

---

````text
# #3162: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[CI run 41985377374](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41985377374) on `bot/issue-3049` (`f18b4f6`, pull_request) had jobs over the 7-minute alert (#73):

| Job | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [db (store contract)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41985377374/job/127105345738) | 8m 39s | success |

Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 5-minute target, not just under the 7-minute alert, so the fix has headroom. Most splits are a count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` (#3072): `web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)` (for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`), or a `rust (test <group>)` group, whose count runs its tests in that many jobs, split by name. A count splits the run, not the compile: a group slow to compile needs its tests in more binaries (the engine's `rules_<n>` each get a job by themselves). Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI.

Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`, and a count or a new `rules_<n>` needs no change there. When the split needs a new group or other flags in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`, or any other change under `.github/`, make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/ci-duration.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-6` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42002190455)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`db (store contract)` took 8m 39s in CI run 41985377374. It must finish well under the 5-minute target, not only under 7 minutes. The job runs `crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`. I timed that script on a 4-core box. The compile took 195 s and the tests 52 s. Compiling the engine and the cards at opt-level 0 for this script cuts the build to 108 s and leaves the tests at 52 s, and the 682 tests all pass.

A count cannot split this job. `scripts/ci-shards.toml` has no `db` table (`.github/ci/matrix.py` only knows `rust-test`, `web` and `e2e`), and a count would not split the compile anyway. So the fix is the script's own build flags.

## Files to touch

| File | Change | What |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/tests/db/run.sh` | change | Add a `PROFILE_FLAGS` variable and pass it to the `cargo build` and to `run_tests`' `cargo test`. |
| `crates/server/README.md` | change | One sentence in the "Tests" section naming the opt-level-0 build. |

**Do not touch:**
- `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/` (the bot may not change them, and no change there is needed).
- `scripts/ci-shards.toml`, since no key there reaches this job.
- Any test file, `Cargo.toml`, `crates/engine`, `crates/cards` or `crates/ai`.

No spec section or ruling governs this change. Do not add a ruling or a pending fragment.

## Steps

1. **Add the flags to `run.sh`.** Put this comment and variable directly above the "Built once:" comment block (just before `echo "--- build (jackioh-server and its store tests) ---"`):
   ```sh
   # The engine and the cards compile at opt-level 0 here, not the test profile's 2 (Cargo.toml): these
   # tests store and read rows and play no game, so nothing runs their code long enough to repay
   # optimizing it. On four cores with the dependencies built, the build took 195 s at 2, 150 s at 1
   # and 108 s at 0, and the tests 52 s at each (#3162). Every `cargo` call below takes the same flags:
   # a different profile is a different build, so one call without them compiles it all again.
   PROFILE_FLAGS="--config profile.test.package.jackioh-engine.opt-level=0 --config profile.test.package.jackioh-cards.opt-level=0"
   ```

2. **Pass them to the build.** Change the build line to the following. Keep the `|| { kill … exit 1 }` block as it is.
   ```sh
   # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # PROFILE_FLAGS is several arguments on purpose.
   cargo build $PROFILE_FLAGS --profile test --manifest-path "$REPO/Cargo.toml" -p jackioh-server --bin jackioh-server --test server_store || {
   ```

3. **Pass them to every test run.** In `run_tests()` change the body to the following. `run_tests` is the only other `cargo` call in the script, and it covers both the `--list` call and the per-shard runs.
   ```sh
   # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # PROFILE_FLAGS is several arguments on purpose.
   cargo test $PROFILE_FLAGS --manifest-path "$REPO/Cargo.toml" -p jackioh-server --test server_store "$@"
   ```
   Do not leave any `cargo` call in the script without `$PROFILE_FLAGS`. The flags change the profile, and a call without them rebuilds the workspace crates at opt-level 2 (about 3 minutes).

4. **Update the README.** In `crates/server/README.md`, "Tests" section, the sentence ending "so that `tests/db/run.sh` builds and links only that (CI's `db (store contract)` job stays under five minutes)" becomes: "so that `tests/db/run.sh` builds and links only that, the engine and the cards at opt-level 0 through its `PROFILE_FLAGS`, which each of its `cargo` calls repeats (CI's `db (store contract)` job stays under five minutes, #3162)."

5. **Leave everything else in `run.sh` alone.** In particular keep `DB_SHARDS` at its default of 3. I ran 6 and 8 databases on the same warm build and the test phase stayed at about 50 s (the 3-database baseline was 52 s), so more shards only add load.

## Tests

No new automated test is needed, because the change is a CI script's build flags. The existing 682 `store::` tests are the proof, and they must still pass. Run these in order:

1. `sh -n crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`
2. `shellcheck crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`. The file already has two warnings: SC1007 on the `REPO=` line and SC2329 on `cleanup()`. The change must add no others, and in particular no SC2086.
3. `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh 2>&1 | tee /tmp/db.log` (needs Docker; the pinned toolchain's first build takes a few minutes).
   - Expect `test result: ok. 228 passed`, `227 passed` and `227 passed` for the three shards, and exit status 0.
   - Then run `awk '/--- cargo test/{f=1} f && /Compiling/{bad=1} END{exit bad}' /tmp/db.log`. It must exit 0, meaning no `Compiling` line after the `--- cargo test` header (only `Finished` lines in well under a second). Any `Compiling` there means a `cargo` call is missing `$PROFILE_FLAGS`.
4. If Docker is not available in the builder's environment, run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store store::` instead. That is the fake-store half, 267 tests, which only proves the code compiles and runs. Say in the report that the Postgres half was not run.

## Done when

- [ ] `run.sh` defines `PROFILE_FLAGS` once, and both `cargo build` and `run_tests` use it (the `--list` call and the shard runs go through `run_tests`).
- [ ] `sh -n` passes, `shellcheck` shows no new warning, and the Docker run (or the fake-store fallback, reported as such) passes with no recompile after the build step.
- [ ] The README sentence is updated.
- [ ] The harness checks pass: `cargo fmt --check`, catalog, patches, rulings (`cargo jackioh spec check`), clippy, cargo tests and the web tests. None of them reads this script, and `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` only maps `run.sh` to `db_store`.

## Risks

- **Flags on some calls only.** A `cargo` call without `$PROFILE_FLAGS` recompiles everything at opt-level 2 and undoes the saving, and the awk check in Tests catches it. Add the flags to any `cargo` call you add later.
- **Cache.** `Swatinem/rust-cache` restores dependencies only, and the flags change only the engine's and the cards' profiles, so the cached dependencies stay valid.
- **Slower tests at opt-level 0.** In my runs the test phase was 52 s at 0, 1 and 2, because the tests wait on Postgres and play no game. `crates/engine`, `crates/cards` and `crates/ai` source and purity are untouched, and no replay or hash is affected.
- **A cold CI cache.** The CI run may have recompiled every dependency, and nothing outside `.github/` helps that. The 108 s is the build's floor on the critical path (engine 46 s, then the server library 37 s, then the `server_store` test 25 s).
- **Measured on a local box, not CI.** The local numbers come from the planner's own box. The CI report that raised this issue also counts checkout, toolchain and cache restore, which the script does not. Read the next `ci-duration` report to confirm.

## Open questions

- **A second pass if it is still slow.** If the next `ci-duration` report still shows this job over 5 minutes, a person should look at the db-suite job's Rust cache first. Splitting the suite into two matrix entries in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` would save at most about 25 s, because each entry compiles again. No `.github/` change is needed for this plan.
- **Left alone on purpose.** `StoreHarness::postgres()` in `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` truncates the tables, and the `reset()` that follows truncates them again. Dropping the first truncate would save about 50 ms of Postgres time for each of the 304 Postgres tests, but it changes the test harness for a small gain. I did not plan it.
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->
````
